# harborpilot_routing_plan_version (Resource)

A version of a routing plan's routing logic (model mappings, restrictions, fallback, privacy, compatibility, intent and engine rules).

With `publish = true` (the default) the version is validated and published, superseding the previous one. Published versions are immutable: changing `document` or `note` creates and publishes a new version. If another version is published outside Terraform, the next plan shows `publish` changing back to `true`, and applying it publishes a copy of this version (a rollback). Destroying a published version leaves it in the plan's history; destroying a draft discards it.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "harborpilot_routing_plan_version" "default" {
  plan_id = harborpilot_routing_plan.default.id
  note    = "Subscription first, API fallback"
  document = jsonencode({
    model_mappings   = [{ match = "claude-*", alias_id = harborpilot_model_alias.coding.id }]
    default_alias_id = harborpilot_model_alias.coding.id
    restrictions     = { denied_provider_ids = [] }
    fallback = {
      steps               = ["retry", "alternate_account", "stop"]
      max_attempts        = 3
      allow_paid_fallback = true
    }
    privacy = {
      policy_id       = harborpilot_privacy_policy.strict.id
      trace_policy_id = harborpilot_trace_policy.three_days.id
    }
  })
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `document` (String) The plan document as JSON (`PlanDocument` in the API reference), usually written with `jsonencode`. Omitted list fields are sent empty: list `fallback.steps` explicitly. `fallback.max_attempts` is required.
- `plan_id` (String) Routing plan id.

### Optional

- `note` (String) Change note recorded with the version.
- `publish` (Boolean) Publish the version (default `true`). `false` keeps it as a draft.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Version id (`pvr_…`).
- `status` (String) `draft`, `published`, `superseded` or `archived`.
- `version` (Number) Version number within the plan.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import harborpilot_routing_plan_version.default <plan_id>/<version_id>
```
